question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $f(x)=3\sqrt{8x}-2,$ we replace $x$ with $8x$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
8x\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8x & \ge 0 \\ x & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\in [0,\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
